newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech shares fall but PM speech taken well-dealers.
newsitem.headline: Czech shares fall but PM speech taken well-dealers.

text.p: The Czech PX50 index fell back again on Friday but a combative speech from Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus pledging to fight on to reform the economy should renew faith in the ailing equities market, dealers said.
The PX50 index dropped 1.5 points to 488.6 led by Komercni Banka which fell 41 crowns to 1,872.

Klaus's speech was called with little warning at the end of a week which has seen the crown depreciate by over eight percent against the mark. The coalition government launched a new austerity package and a new Finance Minister, Ivan Pilip, promising better regulation of the markets, was installed.
The Prime Minister said he would not run away from what he acknowledged was a difficult situation and said current problems could and would be resolved.
Asked what he thought of the speech, Jan Sykora of Wood and Company said:

"I like it. My feeling is that after the elections we saw Klaus wondering where he stands but now they went through the difficult period and now he's coming back. It was something of the old Klaus," he said.
